quotes.text: The most important thing to say out loud is this everything in the data map and the unified catalog is metadata, not the actual data. These tools describe where your data lives and what it contains, and they don't move it or copy it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clears up the most common misconception about what the catalog actually stores.

quotes.text: Data governance means making sure the data you use in reports and decisions is findable, accurate, trusted, and protected.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A compact, jargon-free definition of data governance.

quotes.text: When they change a policy on the data product, it flows down to the assets inside it so they don't have to update every table by hand.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the practical governance benefit of bundling assets into data products.

quotes.text: A steward used to apply policies to one asset at a time, which simply doesn't keep up. As a company grows with active terms, the steward defines the policy once and lets the term do the work across everything it touches.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows why active glossary terms make governance scale.

quotes.text: Microsoft's guidance is that quality is never really finished, because a one time cleanup fixes today's problem and quietly returns next quarter.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear recommendation to treat data quality as continuous work.

Glossary terms and critical data elements

takeaways: Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog is a business-friendly catalog built on the Data Map, and both hold metadata about your data, not the data itself.
Governance domains, data products and active glossary terms let ownership and policies scale with the organization instead of being applied asset by asset.
Data quality rules and scores roll up from columns to whole domains, so owners and leaders can see which data is trustworthy and act before bad numbers spread.
hook: Your company's data isn't missing, it's just impossible to find, so people ask around instead of searching. This Simply Explained episode walks business users, data owners and aspiring data professionals through Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog in plain English. You'll learn how domains, data products, glossary terms and quality scores make data findable and trustworthy.
